job.title: Business Process Analyst
job.description:
ROLE DETAILS

  • $57-$62 per hour + super (DOE)
  • Melbourne CBD
  • Immediate start preferred
  • Office-based role
  • Initial 6-month temporary assignment, with potential to extend 
  • Working Holiday Visa candidates encouraged to apply
  
ABOUT THE COMPANY
This established national organisation is strengthening how knowledge is captured and shared following significant operational change. You’ll join a down-to-earth, collaborative environment where people are encouraged to ask questions, challenge assumptions and find practical solutions. With evolving responsibilities across teams, there is a genuine opportunity to bring clarity, structure and lasting value to the way the business operates.
  
ABOUT THE ROLE
This is a hands-on documentation and knowledge-capture role for someone comfortable working without a perfect roadmap. You’ll spend much of your time speaking with operational teams, uncovering how tasks are currently completed and turning that knowledge into practical SOPs. You’ll investigate gaps, ask questions and help create a reliable source of truth for day-to-day operations.
  
DUTIES
  • Map and document current-state (“as-is”) business processes across operational teams
  • Turn verbal knowledge and informal ways of working into clear, practical SOPs, process maps and operational documentation
  • Capture undocumented business knowledge through stakeholder interviews, discussions and observation
  • Document bespoke operational workflows within the organisation’s knowledge management system
  • Clarify responsibilities, handovers and process ownership across evolving teams
  • Conduct gap analysis to identify missing information, process risks, ownership gaps and areas requiring further clarification
  • Connect information from multiple stakeholders to build a complete and accurate picture of operational processes
  • Challenge assumptions and highlight broader operational impacts, risks and dependencies where required
  • Maintain accurate, organised and consistent SOPs and supporting documentation
  • Support smaller operational improvement and coordination initiatives as priorities evolve
SKILLS & EXPERIENCE
  • Previous experience in business analysis, process documentation, project support, operations or a similar role
  • Demonstrated experience creating SOPs, procedures, work instructions or operational documentation
  • Strong investigative skills with the ability to ask thoughtful questions and uncover information that may not be immediately available
  • Confidence engaging with stakeholders
  • Strong written communication skills with the ability to turn conversations and operational knowledge into clear, practical documentation
  • Excellent attention to detail and organisational skills
  • A proactive, self-directed approach with the confidence to work through ambiguity and determine sensible next steps
  • Experience within contact centres, operational teams or environments undergoing organisational change will be highly regarded
  • Experience with LivePro or another knowledge management platform is advantageous but not essential
BENEFITS
  • $57-$62 per hour + super, depending on experience
  • Take ownership of meaningful work with a clear and practical business impact
  • Gain exposure to operational teams across a national organisation
  • Work closely with stakeholders and build a detailed understanding of how the business operates
  • Join a collaborative team where initiative, curiosity and constructive challenge are valued
  • Melbourne CBD location with excellent public transport access
  • Ideal opportunity for someone who enjoys rolling up their sleeves and creating structure from ambiguity
  • Potential for the assignment to extend depending on business requirements

job.title: Operations Administrator
job.description:
ABOUT THE COMPANY

Join a growing specialist underwriting agency operating within the insurance and financial services sector. Backed by an innovative global specialty insurance group with a presence across Australia, South Africa, the UK and Europe, the business combines the opportunity and visibility of a smaller team with the strength of an established international organisation.

ABOUT THE ROLE

 This is a fantastic opportunity for an experienced administrator or operations professional who enjoys taking ownership, working with detail and being at the centre of a busy commercial environment.

You’ll take responsibility for the day-to-day administration of a growing commercial bonds portfolio, managing transactions from initial issuance through to invoicing, variations, reconciliations, reporting and release. You’ll also become a key point of contact for brokers, clients, landlords and other external stakeholders, while working closely with underwriters and the wider operations team.

Far from a data-entry position, this role requires someone who can think critically, manage competing priorities and spot inconsistencies before they become problems.

DUTIES
  • Manage bond administration from issuance through to variation, renewal, cancellation and release
  • Prepare accurate bond documentation and coordinate digital execution
  • Manage invoicing, premium statements, credit notes and outstanding payments
  • Complete reconciliations and maintain accurate portfolio records
  • Prepare regular bond, premium and exposure reporting
  • Act as a key contact for brokers, clients, landlords and other external stakeholders
  • Partner with underwriters to resolve administrative issues and keep requests moving
  • Maintain accurate documentation and data across internal systems
  • Identify opportunities to streamline processes as the portfolio grows
  • Ensure transactions meet internal compliance, privacy and quality standards
SKILLS & EXPERIENCE
  • 3+ years’ experience in administration or operations within banking, insurance or financial services
  • Strong experience managing high-volume, detail-heavy workflows
  • Hands-on exposure to invoicing, receivables and/or reconciliations
  • Confident communicating directly with external clients, brokers or customers
  • Excellent attention to detail with strong commercial judgement
  • Comfortable working through more complex requests rather than simply following a process
  • Strong Microsoft Office skills, particularly Excel and Outlook
  • Exposure to bank guarantees, surety bonds, commercial leases, legal documentation or commercial contracts would be highly regarded
  • Experience across trade finance, insurance broking/underwriting support, commercial property, lending or credit operations could translate particularly well
BENEFITS
  • This is an opportunity to be part of a growing, dynamic business delivering innovative solutions across Australia, Asia Pacific, Europe and North America.
  • Working closely with an established team of experienced managers within the credit risk insurance business, this position provides exposure to a broad range of transactions and industries

job.title: Senior Compliance Lead
job.description:
• Location: Sydney, NSW
  • Employment type: Permanent, full-time
  • WFH: No WFH, this is a fully office-based role in the CBD
ABOUT THE COMPANY
Lotus People are working with a fast-growing fintech who is on a mission to make life easier for self-employed professionals across Australia, New Zealand and the UK, handling the tax and compliance load so their customers can focus on their own work. 

ABOUT THE ROLE
As the first dedicated Compliance Lead in Australia, you'll build the local compliance function from the ground up. Reporting into the Head of Legal & Compliance, you'll design the frameworks, processes and controls that keep the business meeting its AFSL obligations as it scales. You'll work closely with the Tax Manager, Customer Operations and Strategy teams in Sydney. 

DUTIES
  • Build the Australian compliance framework from scratch, designing new processes, policies and controls as the business scales across Australia, New Zealand and the UK
  • Own the business's AFSL compliance, making sure obligations are understood, embedded and monitored across the organisation
  • Provide second line oversight across payments, AFSL obligations, data privacy, regulatory reporting and AML/CTF
  • Make risk-based judgement calls and put decisions into practice, deciding what can be signed off and what needs to go up the chain
  • Resolve issues and breaches by finding the root cause and improving processes so problems don't recur
  • Review existing controls and automations, testing whether current flagging tools are earning their keep and catching trends nobody has noticed yet
  • Track regulatory change, including Australia's evolving AUSTRAC obligations, and turn it into practical action for the business
  • Support the preparation, review and lodgement of regulatory reports and disclosures, including engagement with regulators where needed
  • Deliver clear, structured reporting to the Head of Legal & Compliance and key stakeholders
  • Maintain accurate, audit-ready policies, procedures and documentation
SKILLS & EXPERIENCE
  • 7+ years in risk and compliance within financial services, including direct experience in a second line oversight role
  • A proven track record of building compliance processes, frameworks or controls, either from scratch or through a significant uplift
  • A solid understanding of AFSL obligations and experience making sure an entity meets them
  • Confidence making risk-based decisions independently, with a practical, solutions-focused approach to risk
  • Strong communication skills 
  • A relevant degree in Law, Commerce, Finance, Risk or Compliance
  • Payments or fintech experience is highly regarded. 
  • Direct engagement with regulators such as ASIC or AUSTRAC is desirable
